items.hook: Rudolf of Habsburg is crowned king of the Romans in Aachen.
items.body: Rudolf of Habsburg (1 May 1218 – 15 July 1291) was a German nobleman and the first member of the House of Habsburg to become King of the Romans, reigning from 1273 until his death. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.body: Keith Brymer Jones and Marj Hogarth are to marry in their chapel home in Pwllheli in May 2027.

items.hook: Concorde makes its last commercial flight.
items.body: Concorde is a retired Anglo-French supersonic airliner jointly developed and manufactured by Sud Aviation and the British Aircraft Corporation (BAC). Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Clio Barnard’s ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ takes top prize at Rome Film Fest
items.body: Barnard’s Birmingham-set drama wins best film prize in Rome’s Progressive Cinema competition.

items.hook: First Balkan War: The Battle of Kirk Kilisse concludes with a Bulgarian victory against the Ottoman Empire.
items.body: The First Balkan War lasted from October 1912 to May 1913 and involved actions of the Balkan League against the Ottoman Empire. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Deep Space 1 is launched to explore the asteroid belt and test new spacecraft technologies.
items.body: Deep Space 1 (DS1) was a NASA technology demonstration spacecraft which flew by an asteroid and a comet. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The White Rose Way is a 104 miles (167 km) walking trail in England from Leeds, West Yorkshire to Scarborough, North Yorkshire.
items.body: It was created in 2011 by local author Paul Brown. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Pendle Hill is in the east of Lancashire, England, near the towns of Burnley, Nelson, Colne, Brierfield, Clitheroe and Padiham.
items.body: Its summit is 557 metres (1,827 ft) above mean sea level. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Chessboards: The Planes of Possibility is a book published by Wizards of the Coast (WotC) in 1993 that is a supplement to The Primal Order, WotC's first publication.
items.body: Chessboards sets out a system for planar construction that can be used with many of the popular fantasy role-playing game system of the time. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The world's longest sea crossing, the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, opens for public traffic.
items.body: The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge (HZMB) is a 55-kilometre (34 mi) bridge–tunnel system consisting of a series of three cable-stayed bridges, an undersea tunnel, and four artificial islands. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Learning the World is a science fiction novel by British writer Ken MacLeod, published in 2005.
items.body: It won the 2006 Prometheus Award, was nominated for the Hugo, Locus, Clarke, and Campbell Awards that same year, and received a BSFA nomination in 2005. One of those things you can't un-know.
